chapter_mission: Wake the three survivors, break Ben's understanding of Jedi history in a single sentence, and get the group moving before the full history can be sorted out. The chapter should feel human first: shock, disorientation, and immediate dependency.
chapter_turn: Ben stops being an investigator with a mystery and becomes the person responsible for three witnesses out of time. He leaves the fortress with a broken version of the Order's founding story and an unnamed enemy already ahead of them.

scene_plan.purpose: Ben and Desh enter the stasis ring and find the shape of the catastrophe in the room itself: twelve chambers, nine dead, three fading, one broken from the inside.
Sera, Torin, and Kael wake. One sentence breaks Ben's understanding of the Reformations, and the scene must let each survivor arrive as a distinct person, not a history lesson.
The group confirms that someone escaped weeks earlier and is already moving. Treat the empty chamber as a live threat, not a solved reveal.
scene_plan.notes_for_scene: Do not identify the escaped occupant yet. End the scene with the group knowing someone broke out from inside and got a head start, nothing more. The name belongs to the next chapter so this one closes on absence, not explanation.

scene_plan.purpose: The group forms because there is no safe alternative. Ben leaves the fortress with responsibility, a direction, and far less certainty than he had when he entered.

relationship_turns.from: dormant — thousand-year stasis, last met at Veranthos
relationship_turns.to: awake and present — recognition, thousand-year ache in the body, no language yet for what's been lost
adjacent — conscripted into proximity without being asked if he wanted it

relationship_turns.from: operational partnership — survey team, Ch 1 dynamic
relationship_turns.to: co-witnesses — both now hold the same impossible institutional fact and neither yet knows what to do with it

exit_vector: The Steady Returns lifts from Gavran's fortress with six aboard. Ben at the viewport. The wrongness has a destination. The antagonist is out there, unnamed — whoever broke out from inside has a weeks-old head start. Ch 6 s1 will give the room her name.
notes: Keep the chapter focused on three human shocks: the stasis ring, the survivors waking, and the realization that the Reformations concealed penance as well as reform. Sera, Torin, and Kael must sound distinct on first contact. Do not dump the full Ruusan history here; hold back the technique, wound mechanics, and Veraine's name. The empty chamber should close the chapter as a live absence, not a solved reveal.
